Manikarnika Films, founded and owned by Kangana Ranaut, stands as a reflection of her fearless spirit, creative independence, and dedication to Indian storytelling. Kangana launched the banner after the success of Manikarnika: The Queen of Jhansi, with a vision to create films that celebrate India’s cultural roots, strength, and individuality.

The production house’s debut project, Manikarnika, set a high standard for historical epics in Bollywood. Despite production challenges and creative differences, Kangana’s leadership as both director and producer ensured the film’s completion with grand visual quality, emotional depth, and patriotic fervor. The attention to historical authenticity in sets, costumes, and performances reflected Manikarnika Films’ commitment to excellence.

Beyond grandeur, the company’s philosophy emphasizes meaningful cinema over commercial compromise. Kangana has repeatedly voiced her intent to nurture new talent—writers, directors, and technicians—through her banner, encouraging fresh voices in Indian cinema. Her later projects under Manikarnika Films, such as Tiku Weds Sheru, further showcase her willingness to experiment with genres while maintaining artistic integrity.

In essence, Manikarnika Films is not just a production house—it’s a statement of creative freedom, self-reliance, and national pride. Under Kangana Ranaut’s leadership, it continues to embody her belief that cinema should inspire, challenge, and celebrate the power of individuality in the Indian film industry.

The Bollywood Art Project (BAP) is a vibrant tribute to Mumbai’s rich cinematic history, transforming the city’s streets into an open-air gallery of stunning Bollywood-inspired murals. Located primarily in Bandra, these larger-than-life artworks celebrate legendary actors, iconic movie moments, and the essence of Indian cinema.

Each mural is meticulously crafted, capturing the expressions, colors, and nostalgia of Bollywood’s golden era. From Amitabh Bachchan’s towering presence to Madhubala’s timeless charm, every piece tells a story that resonates with movie lovers and art enthusiasts alike. The detailing and scale of the murals make them a visual delight and a must-visit for photographers and Instagrammers.

Beyond just art, BAP serves as a cultural movement, blending Mumbai’s love for cinema with street art. Walking through the painted lanes of Bandra, one can truly appreciate how Bollywood is not just an industry but an emotion for millions.

If you’re in Mumbai, taking a stroll through the Bollywood Art Project is a unique and immersive way to experience the city’s artistic and cinematic soul. Highly recommended! 🎥🎨✨

featured_reviews.name: Aditya Ravi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Stopped by on two different occasions to browse the vintage Hollywood posters and ads they have in store.

Thw owner, Hinesh,  and his team was incredibly patient, especially since I had told them upfront that I wasn’t sure what I wanted and was just looking around.

Their collection is fantastic; original Hollywood posters ranging from films of the 1930s to more modern classics. Prices vary widely too, from around ₹500 to a few thousands.

I ended up picking up a vintage Alfred Hitchcock poster and a Charlie Chaplin poster, both of which I’m excited to frame and put up at home.

The staff was never pushy, just helpful, making the whole experience genuinely enjoyable.

I’d highly recommend this store if you’re looking to own original vintage movie posters and memorabilia.

featured_reviews.name: Akash Kapoor
featured_reviews.review_text:
Just wanted to pass along our thoughts on the Bollywood tour as we felt our experience was a little disappointing to say the least for the City + Bollywood Tour.

Starting with the very beginning, the guide was late in the morning. We planned for 9-930 the night before, but he didn't arrive until 10:30am citing traffic as the reason. But as Indians we are all well aware that traffic is the norm in Mumbai and should be planned for accordingly.

A late start means everything was either delayed or rushed as a result. We proceeded with the tour and had to mention each of the viewpoints serving as a reminder whereas I would think it's an expectation that the guide would show us everything without mention. At Taj and Gateway of India we made a short stopover but were wondering that for us it turned out that we had already seen it before but for other tourists how would you expect them to see and enjoy the place in a short rushed time? We then reminded him of Mani Bhawan and other viewpoints, before making our way towards "star homes".

This was definitely the most oversold part of the tour as we saw Shahrukh Khan and Salman's house and Farhan Akhtar. In fact there were other houses on the way that we enquired about to which the guide informed us that it belonged to this celebrity etc, but again I would think this is an expectation, especially when your travellers are Indian. (no kidding, I was able to provide more celebrity addresses on an Ola cab ride) we asked of other houses in Pali Hill and Amitabh's house but it was "out of the way" and also apparently the houses you show depends on where the tour begins which is quite disappointing, a tour should have a proper itinerary.

After the fact, I also reconciled with the word doc and noticed the restaurant we were taken to was Shalimar and not Copperchimney - we were not given an option and once again, this speaks to my point that as the guest I felt like I should have policed the entire route and every fine detail (maybe I should have gotten paid to be the co-pilot). The restaurant was definitely not hygienic as there were fruit flies on pickles and even our drinks but since we were already "late" for the dance we made our way out to SJ. The studio itself is pretty substandard and for serials, yet the guide did a good job to show us around because he was kind enough to arrange us another viewing of another shoot at Filmistaan. At the same time, he emphasized that it was a personal favor though he mentioned the company has relations with studios so they are aware of shoots so not sure if the facts reconciled there and if it really was an additional favor. Such additional favors feel quite burdening so would try and watch the language for guests.

The highlights were the singing studio though again the experience should not feel rushed and feel as if it is not included in the tour but done as a favor. (The guide was kind to ask if any of us sings, but if we said no it would not be a part of the tour... I would expect the tour to be complete as per the itinerary because a traveller would not know what a recording studio experience is like regardless of whether or not they sing).It should be a more organized natural part of the tour as it changes the way one perceives the tour and enjoys it.

All in all, at over $200 per person the tour was not worth the price whatsoever. The car itself was substandard, I'm sure at that cost a newer fresher car can be arranged as it smelled of smoke (cigarette smokes) which is quite disgusting.

featured_reviews.review_text: First off, the location of this place on Google maps is wrong. It is inside the Film city, not outside. This is just the ticket office and where the bus picks you up. We were late but they were nice to call us and then wait for us. There were two half empty buses but no indication which one we should board. We boarded one only to find out later that it was the Hindi bus. So we asked for the buses to be stopped so we can transfer to the bus with English speaking guide. We spent in hour in the bus touring the Film city with only 2 stops. One was the famous temple that is reused in movies by changing Gods. They were getting it ready for a Shiva temple. That was interesting. Everything else was just drive by. Then they brought us to the "theme park" which had some interesting props and some shooting going on that we could watch. We saw Kadar Khan and few other actors. Then there was a very long (1-1/2 hr) live show which included dances by a SRK double. But we were basically made to watch rest of the mediocre show because the buses won't come to get you until the show is over. No one could ever tell us how long some activity is going to take which would have helped set expectations. The first 1 hour of actual tour is fun. Maybe 30 min in the theme park is sufficient. But rest of the 1-1/2 hrs of the talent show is just torture! Hardly anything was in English so we had to keep translating for our daughter who doesn't speak Hindi and also for several non Indians. All in all, kind of OK but could be better and more entertaining.
